As stated before faster speeds. The way it works is let's say you're watching season 4 episode 2 of scrubs and at the part where Dr Cox and Turk remove a lightbulb from a patients ass. Chances are that other people watching the same episode. Netflix will sent out a piece of the video to one person, that client will then copy that info and send it out to a couple more people and those will continue the trend. So Netflix can provide the same service and allow them to send potential higher quality videos out, maybe above 1080p, or 60fps. It also can bypass ISP's throttling service due to information being swapped between clients with a wide range of IP addresses.

Everyone is missing one crucial bit of info:

If you want faster speeds, you will use some of your bandwidth to upload it to other Netflix users.

If you have reasonable Internet, this is not an issue. If you are already in a terrible Internet situation, or using a data plan, this will make Netflix an even worse experience.
